title: FM 3-05.130: ARSOF Unconventional Warfare

title: FM 3-05.102: ARSOF Intelligence

teaching_note: Completed offline provenance case: M1 is a synthetic catalog card for a 1944 institutional manual, M2 a later official republication carrying an explicit release statement, M3 a private 1995 pamphlet and M4 a modern link directory. The completed comparison classifies M1 as catalog metadata, M2 as evidence of the reproduced text and stated release, M3 as private publication and M4 as discovery context; none documents wartime implementation. Withheld M5 shows M1's attachment is missing, so change its content claim to unknown while retaining its catalog date; do not borrow M2's release statement for other files. The case-to-principle result is provenance before interpretation, with no operational reenactment (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]); ageint117 similarly functions as discovery context, not every OSS manual [@ageint118; @ageint119].
title: OSS Origins and Training Manuals (1944)

teaching_note: A historical network diagram is an analyst's representation, not proof of every relationship or a model for organizing one. Distinguish documented contact, inferred hierarchy and claimed continuity, including coercion and civilian harms; generic defensive guidance does not establish a particular network. No clandestine communication, covert organization or security-evasion procedures are taught.
title: Historical underground networks: evidence, coercion and continuity limits

teaching_note: Study the named manual as a historical artifact whose edition, authorship and release need item-level records; an announcement linking a collection does not establish all of those facts. title: OSS Simple Sabotage Field Manual (1944): historical source criticism

teaching_note: Distinguish the historical category and stated objectives from evidence of actual audience effects, moral legitimacy and legal authority.
